closure: RESOLVED 2026-07-31. Closes on the GATE, demonstrated failing. THE PROOF: pull request 5 introduced a deliberate defect in production code - breakingPlan's precedence inverted so PROTO_BREAKING_AGAINST beats PROTO_BREAKING_SKIP=1, the same defect class as MAGELIB-DIV-002, an override silently re-arming a gate the operator disarmed. Run 30660717476: the required `Build and Test` check went RED on TestBreakingPlanSkipWinsOverAnExplicitBaseline (53 pass, 1 fail), `Ecosystem Gates` stayed GREEN because the code still compiled and linted, and the pull request became unmergeable - mergeStateStatus BLOCKED under the org ruleset's required-status-checks rule. Closed unmerged, branch deleted, main never moved off 3bca478. A planted t.Fatal was deliberately NOT used: that proves the runner runs, whereas breaking a real invariant proves the tests have teeth. THE GATE: .github/workflows/ci.yml, jobs `Build and Test` and `Ecosystem Gates`, both required contexts on the magelib ruleset, running `nix develop -c mage -v {build,test,doctor,lint}` on every pull request and push to main. The suite is 54 tests under -race, 0 skipped. -v is load-bearing on both counts: `go test` without it prints a package summary a fully-skipped package produces identically to a fully-passing one, and `mage` without it prints nothing about which dependencies fired, so the log could evidence neither the test count nor that checkHermetic gated anything. Covered surfaces: breakingPlan (a0f10a7), gosecArgs and SharedLintConfig (8d59b7c), Doctor's per-check failure paths and CheckToolchainPin via DoctorConfig.Out (12c208f), mg.Deps(checkHermetic) on Build, Test and Lint (1430285); Doctor, Fmt and Tidy deliberately ungated, the first because a diagnostic that refuses to run on a broken machine is unavailable exactly when it is needed. WHAT WOULD MAKE THIS SILENTLY FALSE AGAIN, recorded rather than solved: nothing asserts `mg.Deps(checkHermetic)` stays wired to Build, Test and Lint - deleting it is a silent regression, because the Magefile still compiles and every target still goes green, and `mage -v` makes the wiring visible in the log without making it enforced. Magefile.go is //go:build mage and outside the package graph, so no test in pkg/magelib can reach it; this is the identical residual GAPI-DIV-044 and GOBLIN-DIV-045 record for checkTerminology. Nothing asserts BufGenerate hands breakingPlan's returned baseline to `sh.RunV` rather than the original `against` parameter - it does, and proving it requires `buf`. checkWorkspaceShape reports `replace target %s missing` for a path that exists but is a file, and discards the os.Stat error, so a permission failure on the parent also reads as missing; both paths are tested and neither message distinguishes them. And the hermetic guarantee stops short of the tools the gate actually runs, which is MAGELIB-DIV-003, opened rather than folded in here.

violation: The hermeticity guarantee stops exactly where the gate's real work begins. CheckHermetic verifies that `go`, `gcc` and `protoc` - plus `pandoc` when it is present on PATH - resolve under /nix/store, then checks the toolchain pin. It does not check `buf`, `golangci-lint` or `gosec`. Since 1430285 wired `mg.Deps(checkHermetic)` to Build, Test and Lint, Lint now guarantees a hermetic Go toolchain and then shells out to three tools none of which were checked: golangci-lint and gosec directly (lint.go), buf via BufGenerate (proto.go). Each of the three could come from anywhere on PATH, including a host install. A host golangci-lint of a different version silently changes what the lint gate enforces; a host buf silently changes the schema treaty MAGELIB-DIV-002 exists to keep honest. What makes this an entry rather than a footnote is the asymmetry: `DoctorConfig.SharedTools` exists precisely so a repo can extend the hermetic tool list, and this repo's own Magefile.go passes buf, golangci-lint, gosec, govulncheck, mage and goimports to Doctor, which feeds them to checkHermeticResolution. So the doctor checks these tools and the gate that depends on them does not - and the doctor is advisory, run when an operator asks, while Lint runs in CI on every push. CheckHermetic takes no parameter through which a caller could close the gap.
rule: build-environment.md (targets run through the pinned shell; hermetic resolution comes from the pinned store); go-project-manifesto (a gate that cannot fail is not a gate - one whose enforcing tools are unpinned reports a result it did not control)
exit: Closes on a GATE, not on a list. CheckHermetic must cover every tool the shared targets actually execute, so that a shell missing one - or a host copy sitting ahead of the store one on PATH - fails the target that needs the tool rather than the target after it. The tool set is data, not a constant: whatever carries it must be the same mechanism DoctorConfig.SharedTools already feeds, so the doctor and the gate cannot drift apart by construction, and it must stay per-repo, because gapi's plugin set is not goblin's. Demonstrated by a run that goes red with a host tool shadowing the store one, not by a commit that adds three names to `baseTools`. WHAT WOULD MAKE THIS SILENTLY FALSE AGAIN, recorded rather than solved: the checked set is a list, and a target that begins shelling out to some new tool does not fail for having skipped it - it simply leaves the list quietly incomplete, which is this entry's own finding recurring one tool later. Nothing asserts the wiring either: per MAGELIB-DIV-001, Magefile.go is //go:build mage and unreachable from pkg/magelib tests, so removing the dep leaves every target green. And checkStorePath falls back to the unresolved PATH entry when filepath.EvalSymlinks returns an error, so a tool whose symlink cannot be read is judged on where it was found rather than on where it points, and a /nix/store-prefixed link to somewhere else passes.
closure: RESOLVED 2026-07-31. Closes on the GATE, demonstrated failing in all three repos. THE GATE: CheckHermetic is now variadic and each repo calls it as `magelib.CheckHermetic(toolchain.SharedTools...)`, where `toolchain` is a single package-level DoctorConfig var that `Doctor` also reads. One value, two readers, so the advisory diagnostic and the enforcing check cannot report different tool sets - which is the drift this entry named. The gate runs from every target carrying mg.Deps(checkHermetic) and reaches CI through required contexts in all three repos. THE PROOF, run per repo and identical in shape: a real executable wrapper for golangci-lint placed ahead of the store copy on PATH. Gated, the target stops at checkHermetic with "golangci-lint resolves outside the Nix store" and the lint gate's own output never appears. With checkHermetic reverted to CheckHermetic() and nothing else changed, the identical command PASSES and the shadowed binary runs the lint - instrumented in goblin so that "it passed" could not be mistaken for "the shadow ran". Restored byte-identical each time and the failure returned. The failure alone would only show a gate exists; the pair shows this change is what made it catch anything. A wrapper and not a symlink, because checkStorePath calls EvalSymlinks and a symlink into /nix/store resolves back and passes. CI: magelib run 30662416726 (60 tests, 3 checkHermetic dependency lines), gapi pull request 32 (5 of 5 required checks), goblin pull request 15 (5 of 5, including Cluster E2E with criu in the gated set). The consumers were bumped to magelib v0.3.0 and re-vendored, proven by grepping the variadic signature INSIDE vendor/ rather than by a green build - go.work satisfies the new symbol from ../magelib even when vendoring did nothing - and confirmed under the mode that ships with `GOWORK=off go vet -mod=vendor -tags mage .`, which plain `go build ./...` cannot do because the Magefile sits behind the mage build tag. Widening the set was safe by construction rather than by luck: Doctor's hermetic-resolution check already ran checkHermeticResolution over the same SharedTools list, so the gate cannot fail where doctor succeeds, and doctor was run first in each repo to confirm it. WHAT WOULD MAKE THIS SILENTLY FALSE AGAIN, recorded rather than solved: nothing asserts `toolchain` stays wired to checkHermetic. Changing that call back to CheckHermetic() leaves every target green and every Magefile compiling, and Magefile.go is //go:build mage and outside the package graph, so no test in pkg/magelib can reach it - the same residual MAGELIB-DIV-001, GAPI-DIV-044 and GOBLIN-DIV-045 all record for their own wiring. The checked set is still a LIST: a target that starts shelling out to some new tool does not fail for having skipped it, it just leaves the list quietly incomplete, which is this entry's own finding recurring one tool later. checkStorePath falls back to the unresolved PATH entry when filepath.EvalSymlinks returns an error, so a tool whose symlink cannot be read is judged on where it was found rather than where it points, and a /nix/store-prefixed link to somewhere else passes. And doctor.go's checkHermeticResolution still spells out the same base-plus-extras concatenation that hermeticTools now expresses, minus the pandoc probe - two spellings of one decision, which is how a divergence of this shape starts.

scope: pkg/magelib/terminology.go (CheckTerminology skip parsing), pkg/magelib/filelength.go (CheckFileLength skip parsing)
violation: Both shared gates can be silently disabled by a plausible configuration value, and the two defects are one defect at two sites: the skip-parsing logic is duplicated between CheckTerminology and CheckFileLength, and it has already drifted. (1) CheckTerminology's bare-name skip branch is unvalidated. Its PATH branch validates properly and carries the correct reasoning verbatim - 'A skip that silently matches nothing, or silently matches everything, is worse than no skip at all: the gate goes quiet and quiet is indistinguishable from clean' - and rejects '.', '..' and absolute paths. One else-branch away, a bare name is taken as `skipNames[n] = true` with no checks. WalkDir's root entry is named '.', so `CheckTerminology(rules, ".")` prunes the entire tree and returns nil. Measured 2026-08-01 against a tree containing the forbidden phrase: with no skip the gate catches it; with a bare '.' skip it reports clean. CheckFileLength guards exactly this case, because the agent building it noticed the hole while copying the pattern - so the ecosystem's newest gate is safe and its oldest is not. (2) CheckFileLength accepts any path as a skip without justification. It rejects a path claimed as BOTH waiver and skip, but a path claimed only as a skip passes unquestioned, and nothing in the mechanism distinguishes generated code the rule exempts from hand-written code someone wanted to stop hearing about. Demonstrated 2026-08-01: moving goblin's 1200-line supervisor.go from its waiver list to its skip list leaves the gate green and silent about the file. A waiver is debt that must shrink; a skip is permanent. Reclassifying the first as the second is undetectable, and a reviewer sees only a line moved between two string slices. gapi's skip has an external alibi in gopy's non-standard header; the next skip added anywhere may not.
rule: go-project-manifesto (a gate that cannot fail is not a gate; fail loudly at boundaries); cooperative-ecosystem-manifesto (shared mechanisms are the contract - a gate the ecosystem depends on must not be disableable by its own configuration)
exit: Close on a GATE, and on ONE parser rather than two agreeing parsers. The root cause is duplication: each gate re-implements skip parsing, they have already drifted, and a third gate would repeat the choice. Extract a single validated skip primitive that every gate consumes, so a skip that cannot mean what the caller intended is rejected once, for all of them, and correctness is not a property each new gate has to rediscover. Two things must then hold and both must be mechanically checked. (1) Every gate rejects a bare skip of '', '.' and '..'. The test is table-driven ACROSS the gates rather than written per gate - a per-gate test is the same duplication one level up and would have let this drift happen again. Demonstrated by removing the guard and showing the test fail, not by the guard existing. (2) A skip carries a required reason, so adding one means stating why the rule does not reach that path. That does not make a wrong reason impossible, but it makes the claim reviewable: 'gopy output, non-standard generated header' is checkable, while a bare path in a slice is not. The waiver/skip distinction only works if the classification is auditable at the point it is made. WHAT WOULD MAKE THIS SILENTLY FALSE AGAIN: a fourth gate added to magelib with its own skip handling, which is exactly how these two diverged - the newest gate is safe only because one agent happened to notice while copying. Nothing structurally prevents the next one from starting fresh, and a shared primitive is only shared while everyone uses it. Note also that requiring a reason string is a breaking API change for both consumers, so it needs a tag and a re-vendor in gapi and goblin, and their existing skip entries need reasons written for them rather than backfilled with 'legacy'.
closure: RESOLVED 2026-08-01. Closes on ONE parser rather than two agreeing parsers, demonstrated failing in all three repos. THE MECHANISM: pkg/magelib/skip.go defines Skip{Name, Reason} and one unexported compileSkips both gates call. CheckTerminology and CheckFileLength now take ...Skip - a breaking change, tagged v0.5.0, with gapi and goblin re-vendored and migrated. The duplicated parsing is gone, so correctness is not a property each gate rediscovers: a gate that accepts a Skip inherits it. PROOF THAT IT IS GENUINELY SHARED, not two copies that agree: deleting the single bare-name guard from compileSkips fails SIX subtests, three per gate, symmetric. Separate parsers would have failed one side. The bad-skip table is written ACROSS the gates for the same reason - a per-gate table is the duplication one level up, which is how this drifted in the first place. PROOF THE ORIGINAL DEFECT IS CLOSED, per repo: passing a bare '.' skip now fails with 'would prune the whole tree' in magelib, in gapi and in goblin. Against v0.4.0 that exact configuration returned nil on a tree containing a violation - the gate silently disabled by one plausible value. A dedicated regression, TestBareDotSkipDoesNotSilenceTerminology, asserts a tree is dirty BEFORE asserting the skip does not clean it, so the test cannot pass by having nothing to find. PROOF THE SECOND DEFECT IS CLOSED: Reason is required and blank is rejected, so a path can no longer be exempted without a stated claim. The two guards are independently load-bearing - removing the reason check fails only the reason rows and leaves the name-shape rows green. The reasons written are claims rather than labels: gapi's names the specific marker mismatch that makes gopy output undetectable to the standard generated-code check, and goblin's records that its deprecation-ledger skip guards nothing today, measured, so an inert skip is labelled inert rather than implying it protects something. That measurement also corrected a count I had asserted: an unbounded grep found three styling matches in goblin's divergence ledger where the compiled word-bounded rule finds zero, because all three sit inside Go identifiers. The gate's own output settled it. WHAT WOULD MAKE THIS SILENTLY FALSE AGAIN, recorded rather than solved. A fourth gate can still declare its own skip parsing; nothing forces it through compileSkips, and only the gates table in skip_test.go would notice, and only if whoever adds the gate registers it there. That is weaker than structural prevention and is the same shape as the residual this entry began as. Second, and created BY this fix: a terminology skip's Reason can itself trip the terminology gate, because the Magefile declaring it is walked - both consumers hit it on the first draft, and goblin avoided it only because the warning was passed along by hand. Skip.Reason's doc comment now states it, which is where the next author looks and is still only a comment. Third, Reason is validated for presence and not for content: 'x' passes. This entry makes the classification auditable, not correct.

violation: magelib's flake enumerates a platform its nixpkgs no longer has. build-environment.md states the explicit system list as a CORRECTNESS REQUIREMENT rather than a preference - 'flake-utils.lib.eachSystem [ "x86_64-linux" "aarch64-linux" "aarch64-darwin" ]' - because nixpkgs 26.11 dropped x86_64-darwin and eachDefaultSystem still enumerates it, so merely instantiating pkgs for that platform throws. gapi (flake.nix:29) and goblin (flake.nix:27) both carry the explicit list. magelib still calls eachDefaultSystem and is the only silo repo that does. GAPI-DIV-035 PREDICTED THIS AND NAMED THE WRONG REPO: its exit records 'NOTE FOR GOBLIN: it still uses eachDefaultSystem with an older lock and will hit the same failure on its next input update'. goblin was fixed; magelib was never named, and no ledger entry has covered it since. MEASURED, and the blast radius is NARROWER than gapi's was - stating it honestly matters more than inheriting gapi's severity. The failure is ALREADY PRESENT, not latent: magelib's current lock (nixpkgs 624af665418d) throws today on 'nix eval .#devShells.x86_64-darwin.default.name', citing the x86_64-darwin-26.11 release note. But nothing in the current workflow forces that evaluation. 'nix flake check' PASSES on linux and reports 'omitted these incompatible systems: aarch64-darwin, aarch64-linux, x86_64-darwin'; 'nix flake show' omits non-current systems without forcing them; and CI only runs 'nix develop -c mage ...' (ci.yml:40,45,63,68), which never reaches darwin. What DOES reach it: any --all-systems operation, an explicit darwin attribute evaluation, and a developer on darwin. magelib also has only one output class - devShells.default - so the doc's SECOND flake rule, that system-independent outputs live outside the eachSystem call, does not apply here: there is no nixosModule to nest wrongly.
rule: goppydae-docs design/build-environment.md ('The system list is explicit, not eachDefaultSystem' - a correctness requirement, because nixpkgs 26.11 dropped x86_64-darwin); cooperative-ecosystem-manifesto (shared mechanisms are the contract - magelib is the build library both code repos resolve through, so its flake failing to evaluate is an ecosystem-wide outage, not a local one)
exit: flake.nix uses flake-utils.lib.eachSystem with the explicit three-system list, matching gapi and goblin. CLOSES ON: 'nix flake check --all-systems' passing, which is the operation that currently cannot complete and the one a plain 'nix flake check' silently omits - closing on a plain check would certify a property the check does not examine. DEMONSTRATED BY FAILURE: restore eachDefaultSystem and show the same command go red on the x86_64-darwin instantiation. WORTH DECIDING WHILE HERE, and deliberately NOT assumed: whether aarch64-darwin belongs in magelib's list at all. gapi and goblin include it, and for them it is arguable - their nix/package.nix declares platforms.linux, so the darwin entry buys a dev shell and nothing else. magelib is a pure Go build library with no package output, so a darwin dev shell is the ONLY thing its list is for, which is a stronger reason to keep aarch64-darwin than either consumer has. Matching the consumers exactly is still the recommendation: three repos with one list is a property a reader can check at a glance, and divergence would need its own justification. RESIDUAL once closed: nothing gates this. Three flakes agreeing is a fact about today, not an invariant - the next repo added to the silo, or the next flake rewritten from a template, reintroduces it with no test failing. A gate would have to live in magelib and read its consumers' flakes, which inverts the dependency direction; the honest alternative is that this entry names the gap and the next occurrence is caught by a human reading a diff.
closure: RESOLVED 2026-08-02. THE MECHANISM: flake.nix:17 uses flake-utils.lib.eachSystem with the explicit three-system list [ "x86_64-linux" "aarch64-linux" "aarch64-darwin" ], matching gapi's flake.nix and goblin's flake.nix. THE OPEN QUESTION, DECIDED: aarch64-darwin STAYS. The entry deliberately left this open and the recommendation held on inspection - three repos carrying one list is a property a reader checks at a glance, and divergence would need a justification this repo does not have. magelib's own reason is the stronger one, not the weaker: it declares no package output at all, so a darwin dev shell is the only thing the list buys here, where in the consumers it sits beside a platforms.linux package. CLOSES ON A GATE, NOT THE ARTIFACT: 'nix flake check --all-systems' now runs as 'Evaluate the Flake for Every Declared System' in ci.yml's ecosystem-gates job, ahead of doctor because it evaluates the shells rather than entering one. The entry's exit named the command; running it once locally would have been a capability nobody invokes again, and restoring eachDefaultSystem tomorrow would have gone unnoticed exactly as it did for the three weeks this entry describes. No ruleset change was needed - the step joins an existing required context rather than adding one. DEMONSTRATED BY FAILURE, AND ATTRIBUTED: on the fixed tree, restoring eachDefaultSystem makes 'nix flake check --all-systems' exit 1 at 'checking derivation devShells.x86_64-darwin.default...' citing the x86_64-darwin-26.11 release note, while 'nix flake check' on THE SAME TREE exits 0 with 'all checks passed!' and 'warning: The check omitted these incompatible systems: aarch64-darwin, aarch64-linux, x86_64-darwin'. The pair is the whole point: two commands disagreeing on identical code is why closing on a plain check would have certified a property the check does not examine. Sabotage restored byte-identical, sha256 verified. PROOF THE DEV SHELL DID NOT MOVE: devShells.x86_64-linux.default evaluates to the same derivation before and after, /nix/store/i9p4f3dy1zx10p59b2hwhhrd7a5cw999-nix-shell.drv, so the change is confined to which systems are enumerated. mage build, test (71 packages/tests reporting), doctor and lint all exit 0 under it, and 'GOWORK=off go vet -tags mage .' reaches the Magefile no './...' check compiles. Resolution modes do not apply here: magelib carries no go.work and no vendor directory, so the lone clone is the only mode it has. RESIDUAL, in three parts, narrower than the entry predicted but not gone. (1) Inside magelib the gate now bites, so the entry's stated residual 'nothing gates this' is false for this repo as of today. (2) It is TRUE for the consumers, and that is a finding this work produced rather than an inherited assumption: nothing in gapi or goblin runs --all-systems. gapi's workflows contain no 'nix flake check' at all, and goblin's only occurrence is a PLAIN check in vm-checks.yml, which this closure has just demonstrated is green on precisely this defect. Both flakes carry the correct list today; both are in the state magelib was in, correct and ungated. That wants its own entry per repo and is deliberately not smuggled into this closure. (3) A repo ADDED to the silo, or a flake rewritten from a template, still reintroduces this with no test failing anywhere - a gate for that would have to live in magelib and read its consumers' flakes, which inverts the dependency direction. The honest position is unchanged for (3): this entry names the gap and the next occurrence is caught by a human reading a diff.

scope: pkg/magelib/version.go (Version); the VERSION file in gapi, goblin and magelib; gapi/nix/package.nix:10; the release workflows in all three repos
violation: VERSION is documented in version.go as "the single source of version truth in the repo" and NOTHING verifies it against the tag being cut. Proven by the act of writing this: magelib v0.5.1 was tagged at 2286cf4f1 on 2026-08-02 with VERSION still reading 0.5.0, and no gate in any of the three repos reported it. THE HIDING MECHANISM IS THE PRECEDENCE ORDER ITSELF: Version() prefers GITHUB_REF_NAME when GITHUB_REF_TYPE=tag, so a tag build reports the correct string and the stale file never surfaces - the rule that makes releases come out right is exactly what conceals the drift from everyone who could fix it. ONE DECLARATION, TWO READERS, DISAGREEING: gapi/nix/package.nix takes the other path, lib.fileContents ../VERSION, with no ref-name fallback. So a gapi tag cut without the bump produces a derivation NAMED FOR THE PREVIOUS RELEASE. Measured, not predicted: nix build .# on 71285440b built gapi-0.1.0-proto2e while the next tag is v0.1.0-proto2f. And it is BOTH artifacts, not just the store path: package.nix stamps core/version.GAPIVersion from that same lib.fileContents value, so the binary would report proto2e too. A consumer asking either the store path or `gapictl --version` gets the previous release's number. Consumers reading either one are misled. NOTE the blast radius is bounded and should not be overstated: Version() does os.ReadFile("VERSION") relative to the WORKING DIRECTORY, so gapi and goblin read their OWN VERSION file and never magelib's. A stale magelib VERSION misreports only magelib's own non-tag builds. THIRD OCCURRENCE, 2026-08-02 evening, goblin: v0.1.0-proto2f was tagged with VERSION stale and the tag had to be DELETED AND RE-CUT - hours after this entry was already open, and after the tag procedure had been written down specifically to prevent it. Three occurrences in four days. The first two were arguably knowledge failures; the third was not, because the knowledge was in hand and written down both times. That is the argument for BUILDING the gate rather than carrying the entry: filing an entry gates nothing, and neither does a procedure.
rule: cooperative-ecosystem-manifesto (a declared invariant with no reader is not an invariant; non-determinism must be identified and bounded); go-project-manifesto (a release artifact must describe itself honestly)
exit: A magelib gate that compares VERSION against the tag ref and FAILS on disagreement, wired into each repo's release path and required, so it cannot be satisfied by a mechanism nobody invokes. DEMONSTRATED BY FAILURE, not by a green run: one tag-ref run RED with VERSION deliberately left stale and one GREEN after the bump, differing only in that file - a single green proves nothing, per MAGELIB-DIV-001's closure. WRITE THE FALSIFIER FIRST: the gate must disagree with the default. A check that reads Version() rather than the VERSION FILE would pass unconditionally on a tag build, because GITHUB_REF_NAME wins the precedence - it would measure the emitter and not the property. It must read the file directly and compare to GITHUB_REF_NAME. RESIDUAL 1: this covers the tag path only. A VERSION bumped to a value nobody ever tags drifts the other way and stays invisible. RESIDUAL 2: nothing asserts gapi's package.nix and the Go ldflags path stay in agreement with each other; they happen to share lib.fileContents today and nothing holds them there. RESIDUAL 3, live debt this entry does not fix: magelib v0.5.1's TREE carries VERSION=0.5.0. THE GATE: magelib.CheckVersionAgainstTag, invoked as `mage checkVersion` from a tags-only .github/workflows/release-guard.yml in magelib, gapi and goblin. It reads the VERSION file DIRECTLY with os.ReadFile and compares it to GITHUB_REF_NAME. It is deliberately NOT written in terms of Version(): that prefers RELEASE_VERSION and then GITHUB_REF_NAME, so a check built on it would compare the tag to itself and pass unconditionally on exactly the builds this polices - it would measure the emitter and not the property. Off a tag ref it ERRORS rather than returning nil, so it is not a Lint dependency and has exactly one caller; a check that returns nil when it cannot run reports success for its entire existence. DEMONSTRATED BY FAILURE, not by a green run. WHAT FAILED WAS THE PROCEDURE, NOT THE GATE. scope: pkg/magelib/common.go:44 (Fmt) and pkg/magelib/lint.go:34-46 (the gofmt check inside Lint); goSourceFiles in pkg/magelib/common.go:22; the generated .pb.go files in both consumers - 9 under gapi/pkg/proto and 8 under goblin/proto
violation: THE FORMATTER AND THE FORMAT CHECK ENFORCE DIFFERENT RULES OVER THE SAME FILES, and the gate's own error message tells you to run the tool that breaks it. Both read the IDENTICAL file set - goSourceFiles("."), which prunes directories via skipDirs and has no notion of generated code, so every .pb.go is in scope for both. They differ in TOOL: Lint checks with `gofmt -l` and fails with "unformatted files (run 'mage fmt')", while Fmt writes with `goimports -w`. Generated protobuf output is gofmt-clean BY CONSTRUCTION - protoc-gen-go emits gofmt-formatted source - but it is NOT goimports-clean, because goimports regroups the stdlib away from third-party imports and protoc-gen-go interleaves them. MEASURED on gapi/pkg/proto/ping.pb.go at HEAD: `gofmt -l` lists nothing and `goimports -l` lists the file. THE OBSERVED CONSEQUENCE, 2026-08-03: `mage lint` failed on ONE hand-written test file, its message said to run `mage fmt`, and doing so rewrote NINE generated .pb.go files that the gate had just certified as clean - churn the developer did not author, in files they did not touch, which `mage proto` then reverts on the next regeneration. The loop is stable and silent: nothing is ever wrong, and the diff never goes away. Blast radius is both consumers, 17 generated files; magelib itself has none, which is why the library that ships the defect cannot observe it - the same shape MAGELIB-DIV-001 named, a rule its author is not subject to. Caught only because the pull request's `git add` named paths explicitly; a `git add -A` would have committed the churn, and the next `mage proto` would have produced the reverse diff with no line to blame.
rule: go-project-manifesto (deterministic behaviour by default; a gate must be able to state what it requires); cooperative-ecosystem-manifesto (one declaration, one reader - two tools deciding one property will disagree)
exit: Fmt and the Lint check must agree on what formatted means, for the same file set, so that running the command the gate names cannot produce a diff the gate rejects or ignores. TWO DIRECTIONS, and the choice is the operator's because they differ in what they promise. (A) ONE TOOL: Lint checks with goimports rather than gofmt, so the gate requires exactly what Fmt produces. This makes the generated files newly UNFORMATTED by the gate's own standard - so it must be paired with an exclusion or the gate goes red on protoc's output, and it puts magelib in the position of overruling a code generator. (B) EXCLUDE GENERATED CODE FROM BOTH: goSourceFiles grows a generated-file predicate, so neither Fmt nor Lint touches .pb.go at all. The manifesto already exempts generated code from the file-length rule, so this is consistent with an existing carve-out rather than a new principle; the cost is that genuinely malformed generated output stops being reported by anything. Detection must be by CONTENT (the `// Code generated ... DO NOT EDIT.` header) rather than by the .pb.go suffix, because gopy output is also generated and does not carry that suffix - GAPI-DIV-044's fileLengthSkips records exactly that gopy stamps a non-standard header, so the predicate must be checked against gopy's output too, not assumed. THE GATE: a magelib test that runs Fmt over a fixture tree containing a generated file and asserts the file is BYTE-IDENTICAL afterwards, plus the converse - that a hand-written unformatted file IS rewritten - so the exclusion cannot be satisfied by a Fmt that formats nothing. DEMONSTRATED BY FAILURE: the test must go red against today's code, which it does, since today's Fmt rewrites the fixture. magelib has no generated Go of its own, so the fixture is the only way this repo can observe the defect at all. RESIDUAL 1: whichever direction is taken, the 17 generated files in the consumers are currently in whichever state the last `mage fmt` or `mage proto` left them; nothing asserts they match their generator's output, so a stale regeneration is invisible. RESIDUAL 2: golangci-lint runs after the gofmt check with its own formatter opinions from the shared config, and nothing asserts IT agrees with either tool - this entry fixes the two magelib declares and does not survey the third.
closure: RESOLVED 2026-08-03 by direction C, which the entry did not list. Fmt now uses gofmt (pkg/magelib/common.go), so the WRITER and the CHECKER are one tool and generated output is left alone BY CONSTRUCTION - no generated-file predicate, no gopy skip list, no -local prefix decision anywhere. THE GATE: TestFmtLeavesGeneratedFilesByteIdentical in pkg/magelib/fmt_test.go, which runs Fmt over a fixture tree and asserts a gofmt-clean / goimports-dirty generated file is BYTE-IDENTICAL afterwards, plus the converse - that an unformatted hand-written file IS rewritten, so the gate cannot be satisfied by a Fmt that formats nothing. It rides mage test, which is the command CI runs. DEMONSTRATED BY FAILURE: the test goes RED against the pre-fix code, with the log line 'Formatting code (goimports)...' followed by the rewrite, and GREEN after the one-word change, logging 'Formatting code (gofmt)...'. A missing formatter FAILS the test rather than skipping it, since an absent test and a passing test are indistinguishable in a summary line. WHY C RATHER THAN THE TWO DIRECTIONS FILED: the entry framed the root as two tools disagreeing, but they disagree because TWO NORMATIVE DOCUMENTS specify different tools - go-project-manifesto.md says Fmt is `go fmt` and that gofmt is non-negotiable, while build-environment.md says `goimports -w ./...`. The code faithfully implemented one doc for Fmt and both for Lint; the contract was self-contradictory. C is a RETURN to the manifesto and needs zero manifesto edits, against six line edits plus two new principles for A+B. Also corrected: this entry's own direction A is not a peer of B - A requires B's exclusion to avoid going permanently red, so A = B + a tool swap, and B ALONE does not satisfy the original exit because goimports would still regroup hand-written imports where the gofmt check looks away. A+B IS RECORDED FOR FUTURE CONSIDERATION (operator decision 22): it is the only direction that makes import GROUPING a merge gate, which C gives up. MEASUREMENT CORRECTED: the divergence is total, not marginal - 9 of 9 generated .pb.go in gapi are gofmt-clean and goimports-dirty, not just ping.pb.go. RESIDUAL 2 FALSIFIED: it claimed golangci-lint 'runs after the gofmt check with its own formatter opinions'. The shared .golangci.yml is version 2 with default: none, a correctness-only enable list, and NO formatters: section - in golangci-lint v2 formatters are a separate top-level key - so it contributes no formatting opinion at all. There was never a third tool to disagree. RESIDUAL 1 SURVIVES: nothing asserts the 17 generated files in the consumers match their generator's output, so a stale regeneration is still invisible. NEW RESIDUAL: gapi and goblin do not get this fix until magelib is tagged and re-vendored into both; until then their Fmt is still goimports and the loop is still live there.

scope: pkg/magelib/lint.go:24 (the ../magelib/.golangci.yml fallback); .golangci.yml; flake.nix's devShell, read by envcheck; .github/workflows/ci.yml (two jobs, both checking out magelib alone); gapi .github/workflows/ci.yml sibling-gates and goblin's identical job, both checking magelib out at main with no ref
violation: MAGELIB SHIPS THREE FILES THAT CROSS THE REPO BOUNDARY UNTAGGED AND UNVENDORED, AND NOTHING ON MAGELIB'S SIDE GATES THEM. The Go code is correctly pinned - consumers vendor a tagged version and a breaking change reaches them at re-vendor time, which is when their own CI runs - and this entry is NOT about that. It is about the files read LIVE from magelib's main: (1) .golangci.yml, located by pkg/magelib/lint.go:24, which searches ".golangci.yml" then "../magelib/.golangci.yml" - the shared config both code repos consume instead of carrying one; (2) flake.nix's devShell, which mage envcheck evaluates across all three shells to compare tool inventories; (3) whatever mage doctor validates as ecosystem pins. MEASURED: gapi's sibling-gates checks magelib out with actions/checkout and NO ref, which is main, then runs mage doctor, envcheck and lint in that checkout's presence; goblin's job is identical in shape. So both consumers execute against magelib's main on every one of their own CI runs. MAGELIB'S OWN CI CANNOT SEE ANY OF IT: ci.yml has two jobs, build-and-test and ecosystem-gates, and both check out magelib alone. A magelib pull request that edits the shared lint config, the devshell inventory or a pin is therefore merged on evidence that says nothing about its consumers, and turns gapi and goblin red the moment it lands - on their next run, attributed to whatever they happened to be changing. THE ASYMMETRY IS THE FINDING: the direction with a formal contract (vendored Go code, tags, re-vendor) is gated, and the direction with no contract at all (files read from a sibling working tree) is not. SHAPE: one-declaration-two-readers, where the declaration is a FILE rather than a value and the readers are in other repositories. FOUND 2026-08-04 while the operator asked whether magelib should trigger gapi CI the way gapi triggers goblin's. It should not, and GAPI-DIV-073 records why that pattern is the wrong thing to copy; the exposure here is real but it is not the one a cascade would address.
rule: cooperative-ecosystem-manifesto (the shared build library is a contract between repos, and a contract with no gate is a convention); go-project-manifesto (fail loudly at boundaries - a cross-repo file read is a boundary)
exit: A DIRECT CONSUMER-GATING JOB IN MAGELIB'S CI, NOT A DISPATCH, and the distinction is the whole point. A dispatch fires after merge to main and reports that something is already broken; a direct job checks gapi and goblin out beside the PR HEAD and runs THEIR mage lint and envcheck against it, so magelib learns before merging. It also exercises the actual change, which a dispatch to a consumer that vendors by tag cannot - see GAPI-DIV-073 for what that failure mode looks like when it is 28% of a repo's CI volume. SCOPE IS THE LIVE-READ SURFACE ONLY: lint against the PR's .golangci.yml, envcheck against the PR's flake.nix, doctor against the PR's pins. It must NOT build consumer Go code against magelib's HEAD - that would assert a resolution no consumer uses and no release makes, and the vendored path is separately proven by each consumer's no-replace-module-resolution job. CREDENTIALS ARE A KNOWN TRAP HERE, recorded so three runs are not spent rediscovering it: gapi's sibling-gates comment states that CI_PAT does not list magelib and that GOPPYDAE_READ_TOKEN is the contents-read token scoped to all three repos. A job in magelib reading gapi and goblin needs the read token, and if it does not exist in magelib's secrets that is the first thing to check. CLOSES ON: a change to .golangci.yml that gapi's lint rejects, opened as a magelib pull request and turning MAGELIB'S OWN CI red - not gapi's, and not after merge. DEMONSTRATED BY FAILURE in that direction; a green proves nothing, because green is what magelib's CI reports today for exactly such a change. RESIDUAL 1: this gates two named consumers by checkout, so a third repo adopting magelib is ungated until it is added, and nothing detects that. The consumer list becomes a second place the ecosystem is enumerated, alongside REPOS in the parent's .paseo/worktree-setup.sh. RESIDUAL 2: it gates the config as the consumers' CI reads it, at their main. A consumer branch carrying a lint fix that depends on the new config still cannot be verified from magelib's side, which is the same ordering problem a shared contract always has and is not solved here.

scope: .golangci.yml (the exclusions entry for adk/python/gapi/native and its comment); gapi .gitignore:55; gapi .github/workflows/ci.yml sibling-gates (Lint Gate); this repo's ci.yml consumer-gates
violation: LOCAL `mage lint` AND CI `mage lint` DO NOT SEE THE SAME FILE SET, so neither a local red nor a local green is evidence about the gate. The instance that exposed it: .golangci.yml carries an exclusions entry for adk/python/gapi/native, gapi's generated gopy binding output, with a comment explaining that gopy's header lacks the canonical 'Code generated ... DO NOT EDIT.' line so golangci does not auto-exempt it. That reads as a carve-out protecting the LINT GATE. It does not, because THE PATH IS GITIGNORED AND UNTRACKED - gapi .gitignore:55 names adk/python/gapi/native/adk.go, and git ls-files over that directory returns ZERO entries. The file exists only on a machine that has run the gopy generation, so a fresh checkout has none. MEASURED, and the measurement was an accident worth keeping: deleting that exclusion produced gapi lint exit 1 with staticcheck findings in adk/python/gapi/native/adk.go in the silo working tree, and Consumer Gates SUCCESS in CI on the same change (magelib #27, first attempt). The CI pass was CORRECT. NO CI LINT JOB GENERATES THE BINDINGS FIRST: gapi's own sibling-gates runs mage lint with no preceding bindings build - the Build Python ADK Bindings step lives in full-build-and-test, a different job - and this repo's consumer-gates does not build them either. So the exclusion is inert in every job that lints, in both repos, and matters only to a developer running mage lint locally after a build. NOT A CLAIM THAT THE EXCLUSION IS WRONG: suppressing lint findings in generated output is correct, and a developer's local run is a real audience. The defect is that its comment describes a gate obligation it does not discharge, and more broadly that the two lint surfaces differ with nothing saying so.
rule: cooperative-ecosystem-manifesto (documentation describes what exists; a carve-out that names a gate it does not affect is a claim about the gate); go-project-manifesto (test behaviour deterministically - a check whose input set depends on whether someone ran a generator is not deterministic)
exit: DECIDE WHICH LINT SURFACE IS AUTHORITATIVE, then make the config say so. THE CHEAP AND PROBABLY CORRECT DIRECTION: keep the exclusion, because a local run is a real audience and generated output should not be linted, and AMEND ITS COMMENT to state that it applies to local runs only, since no CI job generates the bindings before linting. That converts a false claim into a true one and costs one comment. THE EXPENSIVE DIRECTION, recorded so it is a choice rather than an omission: build the bindings in the lint jobs so CI lints what a developer lints, which makes the exclusion load-bearing everywhere and makes local and CI agree. It costs gopy generation time in two repos' gate jobs, and it lints code the manifesto already exempts, so it buys agreement rather than coverage. REJECTED unless someone argues for it: deleting the exclusion, which leaves a developer's local mage lint red on generated output and trains people to ignore it. CLOSES ON: whichever direction is taken, plus a test or a documented measurement that the two surfaces now agree or are documented not to - the artifact must be regenerable, because 'they differ' is a fact about a working tree and will drift. GENERALISATION WORTH CARRYING BEYOND THIS ENTRY, and it is why this is filed separately from MAGELIB-DIV-008: a gate proved locally is proved against the prover's tree. This ledger already records a-clean-negative-is-a-claim-about-the-harness; this is its positive twin, a clean RED that was also a claim about the harness. RESIDUAL: nothing asserts the exclusion is still NEEDED even locally. closure: RESOLVED BY THE CHEAP DIRECTION, which the exit named as probably correct: the exclusion is KEPT and its comment now states the surface it serves. The .golangci.yml exclusions entry for adk/python/gapi/native carries a second paragraph headed 'LOCAL RUNS ONLY (MAGELIB-DIV-009)' recording that the path is gitignored in gapi and absent from every CI checkout, that no lint job generates the bindings first, that in CI the entry therefore matches nothing, and that it earns its keep only for a developer running mage lint after building the bindings locally - so a local lint red and a local lint green are both claims about the local tree, not about the gate. scope: pkg/magelib/env.go (CheckShellUnification, compareInventories, missingTool); the EnvCheck tool lists at gapi/Magefile.go:264-269 and goblin/Magefile.go:214-219; pkg/magelib/doctor.go:78 (checkCodegen, the presence check the plugins DO have)
violation: THE SHELL-UNIFICATION GATE HAS TWO BLIND SPOTS. It is otherwise a strong check: it resolves each tool's real store path inside every shell with readlink -f and demands equality, which is stronger than comparing --version output, and it is CI-enforced in all three code repos. BLIND SPOT 1, FIXED HERE. The probe prints the literal MISSING when 'command -v' finds nothing, and the comparison was 'a != b'. A tool absent from EVERY shell therefore produced MISSING in every inventory, compared equal, and the gate reported success. IT COULD NOT DISTINGUISH 'UNIFIED' FROM 'UNANIMOUSLY ABSENT' - delete a tool from all three flakes and envcheck stayed green. The partially-missing case was caught, but reported as skew with the advice 'converge the flakes and locks', which is wrong for a tool that is simply not in that flake. BLIND SPOT 2, NOT FIXED, AND THE CLAIM IS NARROWER THAN IT FIRST APPEARED. The checked list is nine tools; protoc-gen-go and protoc-gen-go-grpc are in all three flakes and not in it. The first reading of this - that the plugins are unchecked - IS WRONG, and is recorded because the mistake is instructive: a grep of the EnvCheck list came back clean and was read as 'in no check'. They are checked, by doctor's codegen-reachability (pkg/magelib/doctor.go:78, fed by ProtoPlugins at gapi/Magefile.go:34 and goblin/Magefile.go:33), for REACHABILITY ON PATH, PER SHELL. What they lack is AGREEMENT: nothing asserts the three shells resolve the SAME protoc-gen-go. That gap is real - these are codegen plugins, so a store-path difference produces different generated output - but it is a missing agreement check, not a missing check. MORE GENERALLY, NOTHING ASSERTS THE LIST COVERS WHAT THE SHELLS HOLD. It is hand-maintained and duplicated between gapi's and goblin's Magefiles, so a tool added to all three flakes and to neither list is invisible to this gate, with no signal.
rule: cooperative-ecosystem-manifesto (a gate that cannot distinguish success from the absence of its subject is not a gate); go-project-manifesto (test behaviour deterministically - a check whose result depends on a sentinel comparing equal to itself is not deterministic in the sense intended)
exit: BLIND SPOT 1 IS RESOLVED. compareInventories now returns skew and unresolved separately: a tool no shell can resolve, or that any shell cannot resolve, is reported as unresolvable with the shells that lack it, and never as agreement. The MISSING sentinel is a named constant rather than a bare literal. DEMONSTRATED BY REVERTING, which is what makes the green mean anything. The comparison was extracted out of the nix-invoking wrapper first, precisely because nothing about it could be tested while it lived inside a function that shells out to `nix develop`; that extraction changed no behaviour and is its own commit. With the absence branch then removed so absences fall through to path comparison, VERBATIM: 'env_test.go:64: a tool absent from every shell must be reported, got []', '--- FAIL: TestCompareInventories_AllShellsMissingIsNotAgreement (0.00s)'. env.go was restored byte-identical, verified by sha256 (d84bab7420db7eeff9c185c2cb181aba69775033e53488fe1edf7c8a4a6ed30e), and all four tests are green, with mage test and mage lint both exit 0. BLIND SPOT 2 IS DEFERRED, DELIBERATELY, AND THIS ENTRY STAYS OPEN FOR IT. Adding protoc-gen-go and protoc-gen-go-grpc to the EnvCheck lists would be a two-line change, and it would be MEANINGLESS IN CI TODAY. gapi's and goblin's envcheck steps run under GOWORK=off (gapi/.github/workflows/ci.yml:308), so CI resolves magelib from vendor/ at the published v0.6.0 - which does not have blind spot 1's fix. Locally the same command resolves ../magelib through go.work and does. So the tools would be compared by two different implementations depending on where the command ran, and an unresolvable plugin would produce a local red and a CI green. Landing it before the fix ships is how you get a confusing red nobody can reproduce. THE ORDERING THAT UNBLOCKS IT: this fix reaches CI only after a magelib release and a re-vendor in both consumers. Operator decision 28 reserves v0.7.0 for the terminology rule ALONE, so this rides a later tag rather than revising that decision. Operator's call, 2026-08-04. CLOSES ON: the two plugins in both EnvCheck lists, with a CI run of envcheck against a magelib that carries this fix - not a local run, since the local and vendored implementations are the thing that differs. RESIDUAL THAT SURVIVES EITHER WAY: the tool list is hand-maintained and duplicated between two Magefiles, and nothing asserts it covers what the shells hold. Fixing the values does not fix the list. That is the same one-directional shape this ledger has now recorded three times, one level up: the check is sound about what it is given and silent about what it is not.

scope: the published magelib documentation site and .github/workflows/docs.yml: what the site describes versus what consumers build against
violation: THE SITE DOCUMENTS main; EVERY CONSUMER VENDORS A TAG. Measured 2026-08-06: goppydae.github.io/magelib publishes one tree, built from main, with no version segment in any path. gapi and goblin both pin github.com/goppydae/magelib v0.7.0 in go.mod while the published reference describes v0.8.0 and beyond, so the API documentation a consumer reads is not the API they compile against, and nothing on the page says which version it is. THE OBVIOUS FIX IS THE WRONG ONE, which is why this needs an entry rather than a patch: publishing from the tag was tried and is impossible by construction, because an actions/deploy-pages deployment REPLACES the whole site - a tag cannot add itself beside what is published, it can only overwrite it, and the next push to main overwrites it back. v0.8.0 demonstrated it: the tag pointed at main's own tip, so the deploy would have republished byte-identical content, and the github-pages environment refused it anyway.
rule: goppydae-docs design/build-environment.md and the documentation programme's goal 5 (every site is actually reachable - a reference describing code no consumer is running is reachable in form and not in substance); cooperative-ecosystem-manifesto section 5 (documented behaviour is a contract, and a contract has to name the version it binds)
exit: The main build produces every published version as ONE artifact: enumerate the released tags, render each into its own path segment, render main, and deploy the assembled tree in a single deployment. That keeps the site a pure function of the repository - rebuild from scratch and get an identical tree - with no accumulated state and no second deployment to race, which is what rules out the gh-pages-branch pattern where each release commits built output into a long-lived branch. CLOSES ON a published path for a released tag resolving to that tag's reference, asserted by SIZE and not only by presence, since a version loop that silently renders nothing is the omit-rather-than-error failure this toolchain has already produced once. A cap on how many versions are published belongs in the same change: build time grows linearly with them.
